answer: Bind each identity to one physically unclonable function chip: its challenge-response pairs are a fingerprint no factory can copy twice, one flake of shale in a tundra of silicon. A zephyr of cheap scripts cannot fake a PUF response, so a thousand clones need a thousand real chips, each bought, wired, and kept alive. Limit: responses drift with heat and age, so helper data is needed, and a rich attacker can still buy chips in bulk — it should gate rewards, not entry.
